rivals: BUNDLED: provider.Interface metadata, dependencies, palette and Load on each provider
SPLIT: MetricDescriptor static metadata plus Loader execution capability

structural_hypotheses.H_obligation: A metadata-only consumer should not need to receive a Load-capable object. Splitting may lower capability obligations, but introduces registry adaptation cost.
structural_hypotheses.H_congruence: Provider execution and metadata may change independently unlike Swamp's co-required field semantics; the effect need not transport from Swamp's shared-conversion improvement.
structural_hypotheses.H_simple: A simple interface-method count plus changed-site count may explain any reduction. If so, do NOT elevate a new generative ontology.

semantic_checks: old source has provider.Interface with Load, Name, Kind, Description, Dependencies and DefaultPalette
new source has MetricDescriptor without Load and Loader with Load
source revisions are exact and direct parent/child
both revisions run Go provider/package tests independently
disqualifiers: upstream issue names ISP, thus an ISP confirmation is not novelty
historic refactor touches 13 files, not a randomized intervention
test pass does not establish lower lifecycle total cost
same new functional maintenance requirement not yet executed against both source variants
Go dependency/toolchain incompatibility causes HOLD rather than fabricated PASS
claim_ceiling: independent source-grounded architectural mechanism admission only. Need fresh change-sequence test, full S/L/C/A/Q, cross-world conditional prediction and simple baseline competition for any generative OO claim.
